answer: Agents gain voting weight only by locking scarce stake and completing random, time-sensitive tasks tied to a public beacon. Each response is committed with a cipher and checked against later reveals, making copied answers across identities detectable. To mount a sybil attack, an operator must fund every lock and keep each agent active through repeated rounds, tying up capital and paying ongoing compute and coordination costs; identities cannot instantly inherit the reputation honest agents build over time, like nectar gathered flower by flower.
